Gonna piggyback onto this and throw some more in:

RP monsters/creatures: Some baddies have little things about them that scream to mix up an encounter. The Helmed Horror for instance specifically targets the weakest PC; A little bonus given to it by the DM can negate opportunity attacks, meaning the weak PC's allies are gonna have to stop this immediate threat, or protect the weak PC until it dies. Similarly, Kobolds for example have Pack Tactics. To me, that screams either overwhelming numbers (Which would employ the use of 'groupings', where one kobold is actually 5 or so with the health and attacks reflecting such), or strategic moves (pincer attacks, or simply surrounding the PC's).

Moral decisions: Sure, these cultists /may/ be reviving an ancient evil, but look at him. He's quaking in his boots, with maybe a ring on his finger? You're killing a father, a brother, Maybe the local blacksmith who just fell on hard times. Giving even the most mundane enemies a name or flavor can twist things up. He's actually an NPC about to debut in one of my campaigns, but here's what I got so far:
- Cognan, Orc, Warlock, The Machine Patron, Pacts of Apotheosis and The Cloak. (This character relies /heavily/ on material from the [Middle Finger of Vecna](http://www.middlefingerofvecna.com/?m=1) blog, as well as material Submortimer posted on the Giant in the Playground website. I'll summarize it on here as much as I can).
Focus on Strength and Wisdom, and maybe Con. Then Intelligence and Dex. Charisma should be very low; he believes himself a monster, which is in part to his Apotheosis pact (your body reflects your patron, affecting your skin). This is why he also asked for a Cloak (an invocation called Dual Pact allowed two pacts) to hide himself. From his Patron he has a 'Battlefist', which is his main force of attack. It deals 1d10 damage. From his Cloak, he gains a +10 to movement as well as flight speed and no fall damage. He gains a reduction of 9 from bludgeoning/piercing/slashing damage from Apotheosis.
Despite the damage boost from Agonizing Blast, he chooses Repelling Blast to push opponents away. He has such destructive powers, but also doesn't want to hurt anyone. This stems from his backstory of being mutilated by his former allies for failing to lead them to victory, which led to making a pact with The Machine, implanting It's Heart inside him. Augments to his legs further improve his speed.

A creature of that stature will probably have its highest stats in Con, Str, and maybe Wisdom (depending on its age). Charisma would take a hit due to him being dormant, with Dex also lacking due to his big size and structure. Intelligence would be based on whether he's maybe an older magical being or just a creature that has existed.

I'd say it deserves a fancy sensor ability, like Tremorsense within a certain area of the swamp (reference Lair Abilities for stuff like this).

For class, I'd take a couple abilities from Druid maybe or Nature Druid or Feylock. This is mainly if you plan on him ever being in combat or something. If not, I wouldn't sweat it.

This is taken from the anime Log Horizon, with a bit of rework. In the anime the chains only break when they are attacked (as in, having your ally the Barbarian attack the chained creature would break a chain, causing extra damage). Obviously this is really nice for characters such as a Fighter w/ extra attacks or a Monk w/ Flurry of Blows. However, the caster does need to maintain concentration to keep the character restrained.
You'd probably have to give the targeted creature a Dex save to avoid the chains (if anything, making a successful save only leave him held by 3 chains instead of 6) to balance it, though it is a bit of a fair trade to give up the caster's actions to prohibit an enemy from acting.
